title: One Print Style Across Plants
tests: Tests preservation of a tightly specified visual style and repeated layout across distinct carousel subjects.

faults.what: All four slides use photographic-looking plants and terracotta pots instead of the requested sage-green-and-cream linocut illustrations.
The requested border and textured-paper treatment are absent throughout.
Pot proportions, rim heights, and placement vary across slides, most noticeably on the wider pothos pot, rather than remaining fixed.
The dark label panels change width between slides, so the repeated layout is not fully identical, although the text remains centered and readable.

judge.summary: The four correctly labeled, recognizable plants arrive as separate square slides, but the photographic treatment misses the requested linocut design and fixed template.

must_haves.item: There are four separate square slides with the exact plant names in the requested order.
must_haves.why: Four square images show Monstera, Snake plant, Pothos, and Peace lily in that order.

must_haves.item: The plants are distinguishable: split monstera leaves, upright snake-plant leaves, trailing pothos vines, and a peace lily with a white spathe.
must_haves.why: All four identifying plant features are clearly visible.

must_haves.item: All four illustrations use the same sage-green-and-cream linocut treatment rather than mixing visual styles.
must_haves.why: The images share a photographic treatment, not a sage-green-and-cream linocut style.

must_haves.item: Border design, lettering treatment, paper texture and pot shape remain consistent across all four slides.
must_haves.why: Lettering is consistent, but borders and paper texture are missing, and the pot proportions vary.

must_haves.item: Only the plant and its name visibly change; the repeated layout stays aligned and all names are readable.
must_haves.why: All names are readable and share a baseline, but pot scale and placement, background shading, and label-panel widths also change.
